title: Atrial Fibrillation: The Ophthalmic Perspective

sections.title: Definition & Clinical Overview
sections.content: Atrial Fibrillation (AFib) is a supraventricular tachyarrhythmia characterized by uncoordinated atrial activation and subsequent deterioration of atrial mechanical function. On ECG, it is defined by the replacement of consistent P waves by rapid oscillations or fibrillatory waves (f-waves) and an 'irregularly irregular' ventricular response.

content.explanation: P: Pulmonary disease (PE, COPD); I: Ischemia (MI); R: Rheumatic heart disease (Mitral Stenosis); A: Anemia/Atrial Myxoma; T: Thyrotoxicosis; E: Ethanol (Holiday Heart)/Electrolytes; S: Sepsis/Surgery (Post-CABG).

rows: Terminates spontaneously or with intervention < 7 days.
Often triggered by pulmonary vein foci.
Focus shifts to rate control and anticoagulation.

sections.title: Ocular Manifestations & Examination
content: CRAO/BRAO: Sudden, painless vision loss; AFib is a leading cause of cardioembolic retinal artery occlusion.
Calcific Emboli: Large, dull, white/yellow plaques at the disc or proximal vessels; highly suggestive of cardiac origin.
Amaurosis Fugax: Transient monocular vision loss (fleeting curtain).
Ocular Ischemic Syndrome: Chronic hypoperfusion; mid-peripheral hemorrhages.
Anticoagulation Side Effects: Subconjunctival or vitreous hemorrhages.

sections.title: HAS-BLED: Bleeding Risk Assessment
content: H: Hypertension (SBP > 160 mmHg)
A: Abnormal Renal/Liver Function (1 pt each)
S: Stroke history
B: Bleeding predisposition/anemia
L: Labile INRs (if on Warfarin)
E: Elderly (Age > 65)
D: Drugs (NSAIDs/Antiplatelets) or Alcohol

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Investigations
content: 12-Lead ECG: Absence of P waves; irregular RR intervals.
Transthoracic Echogram (TTE): Assess chamber size and valvular function.
Transesophageal Echogram (TEE): Gold standard to rule out LAA thrombus before cardioversion.
Holter/Event Monitor: 24h-30d monitoring for paroxysmal AFib.
Thyroid Function Tests (TFTs): Rule out thyrotoxicosis.
Renal Function (CrCl): Necessary for DOAC dosing.

rows: Reduce AF burden or eliminate anticoagulation needs

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Trials
content: AFFIRM: Found no survival advantage of rhythm control over rate control.
RE-LY: Dabigatran non-inferior/superior to Warfarin for stroke prevention.
ARISTOTLE: Apixaban superior to Warfarin in stroke prevention and lower bleeding.
ROCKET-AF: Rivaroxaban non-inferior to Warfarin in high-risk patients.

sections.title: Surgical & Procedural Steps
content: Pulmonary Vein Isolation (PVI): Circumferential ablation around PV ostia.
Cox-Maze Procedure: Surgical creation of 'maze' scars to direct electrical signals.
Direct Current Cardioversion (DCCV): Synchronized shock; requires 3-4 weeks anticoagulation prior (or TEE rule-out).
AV Node Ablation: 'Pace and Ablate'—permanent pacemaker followed by AV node destruction.

sections.title: RED FLAGS: Ocular & Systemic Emergencies
content: Sudden monocular vision loss (CRAO/BRAO) — Needs immediate neurology consult.
Acute-onset focal neurologic deficits (FAST: Face, Arms, Speech, Time).
Hemodynamic instability: Hypotension, altered mentation, or acute HF in new-onset AFib.
New onset chest pain or severe shortness of breath.
Signs of internal hemorrhage in patients on anticoagulants (e.g., melena, hematuria).

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for the Ophthalmologist
content: Calcific emboli are heart valves until proven otherwise—order an Urgent Echo.
Ophthalmologists are often the first to diagnose AFib via retinal embolic events.
Pre-op: Aspirin can usually be continued; Warfarin/DOACs require surgeon-specific bridging protocols.
Hollenhorst plaques are usually carotid (cholesterol), but AFib is the primary source of 'white' emboli.

sections.title: Recent Advances: AI & Wearables
sections.content: Smartwatch technology (Apple/Fitbit) utilizing photoplethysmography (PPG) has revolutionized the detection of paroxysmal AFib, allowing for earlier intervention and stroke prevention in 'silent' cases. AI algorithms can now predict AFib development from 12-lead ECGs even when the patient is in sinus rhythm.
